policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Thou art Jehovah' renders the 2ms pronoun; qere אַתָּה and ketiv את differ only in orthography of the same pronoun, and the English cannot distinguish the spellings. No mapped note. Base qere fallback retained.

ASV 'slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness' renders רַב־חֶסֶד as a construct chain: 'in' subordinates lovingkindness to 'abundant' with no conjunction between them. The ketiv וחסד would coordinate lovingkindness as a separate item ('abundant, and lovingkindness'), which the English does not do. The only mapped note (hebrew_gloss on 'ready to pardon') concerns סְלִיחוֹת, not this unit.
